47014cdb-9eac-5a82-996c-6ec26344f46f.title: Finding an Expression for the Current

e-21893.knowledge_point: Finding an Expression for the Current
e-21893.problem:
The charge $q(t)$ on the capacitor, in coulombs, in a series RCL circuit at time $t$ seconds is

$$
q(t) = 4e^{-3t} - 2e^{-t} + \dfrac5{17}\cos(2t) + \dfrac3{17}\sin(2t).
$$

Find, in amperes, the exact amplitude of the steady-state **current** $I$ in this circuit.
e-21893.worked_solution:
The current $I$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q$ measured in coulombs.

$$
I = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}q}{\mathrm{d}t}
$$

Differentiating the given expression for $q(t),$ we obtain the following expression for $I,$ in amperes:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(t) & =\frac{d}{dt}(4{e}^{-3t}-2{e}^{-t}+\frac{5}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\frac{3}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) \\  & =-12{e}^{-3t}+2{e}^{-t}-\frac{10}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\frac{6}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).\end{aligned}
$$

Note the following:

- The quantity $I_c(t) = -12e^{-3t} + 2e^{-t}$ is the *transient current*, since it goes to zero as $t \to \infty.$

- The function $I_p(t) = -\dfrac{10}{17}\sin(2t) + \dfrac{6}{17}\cos(2t)$ is the *steady-state current*. It governs the current's long-term behavior.

Therefore, as $t\to\infty,$ we have

$$
I(t)\approx I_p(t) = -\dfrac{10}{17}\sin(2t) + \dfrac{6}{17}\cos(2t).
$$

Finally, the amplitude of the steady-state current, in amperes, is given by

$$
\sqrt{\left(-\dfrac{10}{17}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{6}{17}\right)^2}
= \sqrt{\dfrac{136}{289}}
= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{2\sqrt{34}}{17}}.
$$
